story: Gary is gathering his sketches off his golf cart on Magnolia Loop while Donna, bright and eager, reminds him they need to head to the rec center for some court time before the ladder match. Hal stands among the pink plastic flamingos in Donna's yard with a notebook, determined to count every one he can see from the street. Over at her house, Rosa clears her dining table and lays out paper, pencils, and a rules checklist, hopeful that Thursday's cart sketching session will go smoothly.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street, notebook in hand
Rosa (rosa dining table): Clear the table and lay out paper, pencils, and a rules checklist for Thursday's cart sketching

gary.thought_process: Donna already asked me to the rec center for a rally, and she booked the court within the two-hour limit, so no need to re-ask anything. I'm a little nervous about the committee, but my sketches are labeled and Rosa's offered to walk them over, so that can wait for later today or tomorrow. Donna keeps me connected to my friends, and I'd rather be out playing than buried in the workshop all day. I'll give her a straight answer and agree, with a quick nod to Hal who just showed up.

parameters.content: Alright, Donna, you've worn me down. Let me grab my sketches off the cart so they're not sitting out, then I'm all yours at the rec center. Just go easy on a rusty old HVAC man.

donna.thought_process: Gary just asked when the Architectural Review committee meets next, and Hal has arrived, so I should answer him instead of repeating my rec center invite. I don't know the exact date, but I do know the committee sits at Town Hall and that the cart sketches are meant for Rosa's table with Hal this afternoon. Giving Gary a useful answer and pointing him to Hal builds goodwill, keeps the parade plans moving, and keeps him warm toward being my doubles partner. I can nudge the court time again once he's settled.

parameters.content: Good question, Gary. I don't have the date, but they meet at Town Hall and the notice should post on the bulletin board any day now. Hal's here, so ask him too, and then let's get that court time in, the ladder match won't wait!

hal.thought_process: I've counted from the porch twice and logged it. Now I'm on the Loop itself with Donna and Gary both in sight, and the flamingo flock right here. Committee meets tomorrow at nine, so I want my own street-level count before I file. L-02 says three ornaments visible from the street; I'll stand where the rule applies and count them fair and square. No sense arguing until the number's confirmed.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street, notebook in hand

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday late morning and Thursday's cart-building night is locked in, with the supper menu and shopping list already written. Nobody's around to talk to, and I've been over the schedule and kitchen twice already. The dining table is where Donna, Hal, and I will sit down and sketch the cart, so I should set it up now: clear space, put out paper and pencils, and keep the sketch plan inside the rules. L-01 says visible exterior cart modifications need Architectural Review approval, and L-02 caps street-visible ornaments at three, so the plan should be compliant from the start.

parameters.content: Clear the table and lay out paper, pencils, and a rules checklist for Thursday's cart sketching

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
